hints: Recall which quark family the top quark belongs to - up, charm and top are the $+\frac{2}{3}e$ group, while down, strange and bottom are the $-\frac{1}{3}e$ group.
Remember the antiparticle rule: an antiquark has the same magnitude of charge as its quark but the opposite sign.
Combine the top quark charge with the sign change to predict the anti-top charge before checking the four fractions of $e$.
walkthrough: Identify the particle: top is an up-type quark, in the same group as up and charm.
State the quark charge rule: up-type quarks each have charge $+\frac{2}{3}e$, so top quark charge $= +\frac{2}{3}e$.
State the antiparticle rule: charge reverses sign, so $q_{anti} = -q_{quark}$.
Match to the options: this value corresponds to $-\frac{2}{3}e$. This is option A.

options.A: The top quark has charge $+\frac{2}{3}e$, so its antiparticle has the opposite charge $-\frac{2}{3}e$.
options.B: Charge $-\frac{1}{3}e$ belongs to anti-up-type is wrong; it is the charge of down, strange and bottom quarks, not an anti-top.
options.C: Charge $+\frac{1}{3}e$ is the charge of an anti-down-type quark such as anti-down, not an anti-top quark.
options.D: Charge $+\frac{2}{3}e$ is the charge of the top quark itself; the anti-top must have the opposite sign.
